title: Refusing to disco-fy his music
summary: A record company wants disco; he insists on authentic Afro-Cuban identity.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: I must put in my music that strong boom boom boom boom (unintelligible). You got a disco, and the disco going good, keep it up. If I play Cuban music, I'm going to play Cuban music. Don't do like we always do in this country, because everybody here is nothing but money-crazy, and they can change their mind before the moon change. Everything is a monopoly here and this thing sells now, and as soon as somebody sell it, everybody go and try to change everything and do it another way.

Regardless of -- no conception whatsoever, no, no, no, no. They'll __________ anything to get into the dollar. I don't want to be used that way. My music is something that I've been working for so many years, to be able to present it to this country, even with a whole lot of __________, but never to lose the authentic identity, the Afro-Cuban, no matter how much jazz I put on the top and no matter how much symphonic music I put on the top. But the thing on the bottom I made sure it was always playing Afro-Cuban rhythms.
